description: Shared chemistry rules. C++ ctest (smsd_chemistry_rules_golden_tests), Java JUnit (ChemistryRulesGoldenTest) and Python pytest (test_chemistry_rules_golden.py) read this file, so a rule that drifts in one language fails in every language. Expected values follow the stated rule; fingerprint bits are the published bits, which must not change.

similarity.rule: Tanimoto |A&B|/|A|B| and overlap |A&B|/min(|A|,|B|) score 1.0 for two empty fingerprints (identical empty sets); one empty fingerprint scores 0.0. Dice scores 0.0 for two empty fingerprints and cosine scores 0.0 when either is empty. Soergel is 1 - Tanimoto. An empty fingerprint given as zero words or as no words is the same set.

fingerprint_quality.rule: A fingerprint of fp_size bits N with s distinct bits set, here positions 0 to s - 1, has density s/N. Hashing n features into N bits sets N(1 - (1 - 1/N)^n) bits on average, so s set bits suggest n = ln(1 - s/N) / ln(1 - 1/N) features; expected_collision_rate is the share 1 - s/n of them that fell on a bit already set, 0 when no bit and 1 when every bit is set. is_saturated is a density above 0.75.

circular_similarity.rule: Batch similarity is the Tanimoto coefficient of ECFP fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits); an empty molecule has an empty fingerprint.

implicit_hydrogens.rule: SMILES valence model: aromatic bonds count once and an aromatic atom counts one more bond order; a neutral aromatic atom already at its lowest default valence takes none. The smallest default valence that fits sets the count; cations of N, P, O, S, As and Se and anions of B and Al gain |charge|, other charged atoms lose it. Elements without a default valence take none.

smarts.rule: SMARTS H is total hydrogen count, X total connectivity and v total valence (aromatic bonds once, plus one Kekule double bond for an aromatic atom below its lowest default valence). Expected atoms match the single-atom pattern.

smarts_without_hydrogen_counts.rule: A graph built without hydrogen counts takes the implicit-hydrogen rule above, so SMARTS H, X and v agree with the parsed molecule wherever the valence model holds.

tautomer_confidence.rule: A query atom is relaxed when its element or aromaticity differs from its target atom, or when it ends a selected bond whose order or aromaticity differs. Confidence is the geometric mean, over relaxed atoms with a tautomer class in either molecule, of the smaller baseline weight in the solvent and pH context; 1.0 when nothing is relaxed. Each atom of a class takes the weight of the first motif, in a fixed priority order, whose pattern covers it, whatever the order of the atoms, and the ionisable site and aqueous pKa, applied in every solvent, that the matches of that motif carry: a match carries the acid site of its motif only when the atom that would release the proton (the N-O oxygen of a hydroxamic acid; the nitrogen of an imide, urea, amide or thioamide; the alpha carbon of a ketone or thione and the bridging carbon of a 1,3-diketone; the nitrogen or oxygen of a pyridone or pyridinone; a phenol oxygen with no second heavy-atom neighbour) bears a hydrogen or, when that atom belongs to an earlier motif, the site of that motif. The solvent shift comes first; the pH then scales the weight of an atom with an ionisable site by the neutral fraction of its class, 1 / (1 + 10^(pH - pKa_a) + 10^(pKa_b - pH)) with pKa_a the lowest acid pKa and pKa_b the highest base pKa among the sites of the class, without the term of a kind of site the class lacks, clamped to [0.1, 0.99]; an atom without a site keeps its weight at every pH. A case with same_as is a comparison named there with the atoms of a molecule in another order, and its confidence must equal that of the named case within the tolerance. The three-argument form selects every mapped bond present in both molecules (the induced bonds used here) and applies the tautomer profile in water at pH 7.4. Out-of-range atoms are rejected.

path_fingerprints.rule: path_fingerprint hashes the atomic-number sequence of each heavy-atom path of up to path_length bonds; batch_fingerprint hashes atom labels and bond orders over all atoms with fp_size rounded up to whole words; mcs_fingerprint hashes atom and bond invariants over heavy atoms. Bits are published and must not change.

tetrahedral_centres.rule: A tagged atom is a tetrahedral centre when it has four neighbours and no implicit hydrogen, or three neighbours and either one implicit hydrogen or, for N, P, S, As, Se, Sb and Te, none (its lone pair is the fourth ligand). Hydrogen counts not supplied follow the valence model. The tag winds the ligands in order: the neighbours in order, with the implicit ligand second when the first neighbour precedes the atom and first otherwise; ligands is that order, with -1 for the implicit ligand, or null for an atom that is not a centre. SMILES tags on atoms that are not centres are dropped. Tag 1 is anticlockwise (@) and 2 clockwise (@@). Chiral substructure matching compares centres by their mapped ligands, and labels are the CIP descriptors.

smarts_daylight.rule: Daylight SMARTS. A bracket atom of an optional isotope, H, an optional charge and an optional atom class, and nothing else, is a hydrogen atom ([H], [2H], [H+], [H:1]); elsewhere H is a hydrogen count ([CH], [H1], [H,C]). r<n> is the size of the smallest ring through the atom. R<n> counts the rings through the atom of a smallest set of smallest rings that holds as many rings as the cycle rank, so the six central atoms of coronene are R3. A pair of directional bonds constrains the bond between their atoms: a double bond must have the configuration they give, and an aromatic bond or a double bond without a configuration matches only when either is written with ? (/? or \?); /,\ accepts either configuration but not none. A directional bond is a single, non-aromatic bond; without a configured double bond beside it, it matches in either direction. Atoms within one top-level ( ) group match atoms of one target component, and atoms of different groups atoms of different components. @ and @@ match an atom with that configuration of its mapped neighbours; @? and @@? also match an atom without a configuration, and a query atom whose pattern neighbours do not define a configuration matches either configuration of a configured atom. A ring closure written with a bond at both ends must give the same bond expression at each, and no direction (/ or \) at either, since a direction at the closing digit is read from the closing atom, as it is when written at the closing digit alone, so F/C=C1.Cl/1 is the cis isomer; rejected lists the patterns that are therefore invalid. embeddings is the number of mappings matchAll returns.

cip_mancude.rule: CIP digraphs give a ring atom with exactly one double bond one duplicate atom for that bond. In a mancude ring system, those atoms left after repeatedly removing the ones with fewer than two of them as ring neighbours, the duplicate of a double bond within the system takes the mean atomic number of the atom's ring neighbours in the system whenever their sum differs from the double bond partner's atomic number times their count, even when that mean is a whole number, and the double bond partner otherwise (IUPAC 2013 P-92.1.4.4). Labels therefore do not depend on the Kekule structure, the atom order or whether the input is written aromatic. labels are the R/S descriptors by atom; a molecule whose ligands are equal under this rule has none. Expected labels were checked against an independent CIP implementation.

aromatic_input.rule: Aromaticity is perceived from the structure whether the input writes a ring aromatic or with Kekule bonds, as RDKit and CDK read it: atoms written aromatic and joined by aromatic bonds first take a Kekule structure and are then perceived again, so a ring written aromatic that the model does not find aromatic loses its flags. Atoms written in capitals but joined by : ring bonds are read as aromatic atoms, as aromatic_bond_hydrogens states. A carbanion with three sigma bonds contributes two electrons, whether written with aromatic or Kekule bonds; one with two sigma bonds, such as phenide, contributes only a ring pi bond, and a carbocation none. aromatic_atoms is the number of aromatic atoms of the parsed graph, in the Java library after Standardiser.standardise.

cip_hierarchical_ranking.rule: A first pass ranks the ligands of a tetrahedral centre, and the two ligands at each end of a double bond, by Rule 1a alone (IUPAC 2013 P-92.1.3). Ligands it leaves tied are ranked over the hierarchical digraph by Rule 1b (a ring-closure duplicate whose original is nearer the root first), then Rule 2, then Rule 3 and, for a centre, Rules 4 to 6, each rule read sphere by sphere over the whole digraph before the next is consulted. A ring-closure duplicate therefore outranks an isotope or a double-bond configuration further out, and a double bond whose ends are told apart only by another double bond is labelled by Rule 3. Double bonds are labelled by Rules 1 to 5, so like descriptor pairs outrank unlike ones at an end (Rule 4b); a double bond whose ligands at one end are told apart only by Rule 5 is unlabelled. labels are the R/S descriptors by atom and bonds the E/Z descriptors by atom pair; every other tagged atom and annotated double bond is unlabelled. Expected labels were checked against an independent CIP implementation.

chemistry_profiles.rule: ChemOptions.profile(name) ignores the case of the name. Every named profile and the tautomer profile start from the defaults below and change only the fields listed; every other field keeps its default in all three languages.

similarity_upper_bound.rule: similarityUpperBound labels each atom by element, by aromaticity as well under strict aromaticity, and by ring membership as well when ring atoms match ring atoms only; without element matching every atom shares one label. The bound is the number of atoms the two molecules pair by label, divided by the atoms of the union. Charges, isotopes, stereochemistry, ring fusion and tautomer awareness do not change the labels, so tautomer-aware matching keeps elements apart. Reversing the molecules gives the same value.

consensus.rule: MCS.consensus reduces each input in turn as a seed: the seed, and then its common subgraph with every other input taken in input order, each intersected with the graph reduced so far, are candidates. A candidate is kept when it is a valid common graph under the options and embeds (induced for MCIS) in at least ceil(threshold * n) inputs; the first candidate with the best score wins, so the source index follows the input order. The mappings are keyed by the supporting inputs, the seed included.

aromatic_bond_hydrogens.rule: An explicit aromatic bond (:) in a ring is aromatic, so both its atoms are aromatic whatever case their symbols are written in, as RDKit reads them: an atom written in capitals but joined to its ring by : takes the hydrogens of an aromatic atom, so C1:C:C:C:C:C:1 is benzene and C1:C:C:N:C:C:1 pyridine, while an atom in brackets keeps the hydrogens written for it. Outside a ring, : is read as a single bond. An aromatic bond counts once in the bond order sum and an aromatic atom one more, as the valence model above. hydrogens are the implicit hydrogen counts by atom; C++ and Java agree on every input.

stereo_embeddings.rule: A substructure search embeds the query, so with use_chirality a tagged query centre needs a tagged target centre of the same winding over the mapped ligands, and with use_bond_stereo a configured query double bond needs a configured target bond of the same relation, as a SMARTS chirality primitive or pair of directional bonds does; an untagged or unconfigured query atom or bond matches any target. A common-subgraph search keeps an unspecified target atom or bond as a wildcard: atoms is the size of the best match under the same options.

tautomer_consistency.rule: validateTautomerConsistency conserves the mobile hydrogens of the mapped N, O and S atoms within each tautomer class: each atom contributes its hydrogen count, the stored count or the valence model's, whatever the orders of its bonds, so an aromatic N-H counts one hydrogen. atoms are the mapped query-target pairs and consistent the result.

tautomer_classes.rule: Every tautomer motif pattern is evaluated over all of its matches. The atoms of one match share a class, and matches that share an atom join their classes, so atoms that interconvert through any chain of motifs form one class (the union-find closure of the matches) and the partition does not depend on the atom order. The classes are numbered in increasing order of a key, the sorted colours of their atoms, where each colour starts from the element, charge, mass number, hydrogen count, aromaticity, ring membership, degree and motif cover of the atom and is refined Weisfeiler-Leman fashion by the bond orders and colours of its neighbours until the keys differ or the colours stop splitting; of classes that still share the smallest key, which the refinement cannot tell apart (in practice those a symmetry of the graph exchanges), the one with the lowest atom index takes the next number, its atoms are given colours of their own and the refinement resumes. classes gives each atom's class, -1 outside every class; a molecule written in another atom order has the same partition, and the same numbers except among classes that the refinement cannot tell apart.

murcko_scaffolds.rule: The Murcko scaffold keeps the ring atoms, the atoms on the paths between rings and every atom joined to one of these by a double or triple bond, with that bond, in input order; double-bonded atoms are kept as in Bemis and Murcko (1996) and RDKit. Rings stay whole, so the ring and aromaticity perception of the input is kept. A stereocentre keeps its configuration when all its neighbours stay, and a double bond when each end keeps a ligand. A stripped substituent is replaced by hydrogen: a scaffold atom that lost neighbours takes the valence model's hydrogen count for its remaining bonds, and an aromatic N or P its count plus one per stripped neighbour. hydrogens are the implicit hydrogen counts of the scaffold atoms and scaffold its canonical SMILES.

consensus_native_order.rule: MCS.consensus seeds a candidate from each input in turn: the input itself, then its common subgraph with each other input in input order, found with the search of match. Each candidate is embedded in every input, induced for an MCIS, to count its support, and a candidate the options reject is not considered. The best supported candidate by the objective (bonds then atoms for an MCES, atoms then bonds for an MCIS) is kept, and a later candidate of equal score does not replace it. source_index is the input of the kept candidate, atoms its atoms in that input, support the inputs that embed it and smiles its canonical SMILES; nothing found gives source_index -1. Excluded target atoms and atom weights are rejected.

cip_auxiliary_descriptors.rule: A centre whose ligands Sequence Rules 1 to 3 leave tied is ranked by Rules 4 and 5 over its hierarchical digraph (IUPAC 2013 P-92.1.3). Every other stereogenic unit in the digraph takes an auxiliary descriptor at each of its nodes, found with the digraph re-rooted at that node and the nodes labelled from the deepest sphere inwards. Rule 4a ranks R and S before r and s before none, Rule 4b like descriptor pairs before unlike (each branch read against the majority descriptor of its first sphere with any), Rule 4c r before s and Rule 5 R before S; a centre told apart only by Rule 5, or by the Rule 6 reference, is pseudoasymmetric and takes the lower-case r or s. Rule 2 reads an unlabelled atom at its standard atomic weight, in both passes, so an isotope lighter than that weight ranks below the unlabelled element. labels are the descriptors by atom; every tagged atom without one is left unlabelled. Expected labels were checked against an independent CIP implementation.

fingerprint_options.rule: FingerprintOptions gives the same bits and counts in C++, Java and Python. options lists the keyword arguments applied to the classic configuration of the family (FingerprintOptions.of(family) in C++ and Java, FingerprintOptions(family=...) in Python); maccs selects the 166 MACCS keys. A classic case must also equal the fixed function of its family. bits are the set positions and counts the non-zero (position, count) pairs; same_bits_as names a case with identical bits. Stereo descriptors join the circular hashes after the first iteration, so enantiomers and E/Z isomers differ only where a centre or a stereogenic bond lies; double bonds in rings of fewer than eight atoms carry no E/Z. The framework keeps ring atoms, linkers and the atoms double- or triple-bonded to them, caps the rest with hydrogen and re-reads surviving tetrahedral tags and double-bond configurations. The ring terms read a smallest set of smallest rings that holds as many rings as the cycle rank, so coronene counts seven aromatic rings. Bits are published and must not change.

strict_ring_fusion.rule: Strict ring fusion compares per-atom ring membership counts from bounded Horton candidates in neighbour-index order, retaining the 8.0.x definition. These counts are separate from the full relevant-cycle set. An incomplete count-producing perception prevents a proved strict result.

double_bond_ligands.rule: With use_bond_stereo, a ligand of an end of a configured double bond is a mapped neighbour joined to that end by a selected bond. In a three-membered ring the third atom neighbours both ends, and is a ligand only of the end whose bond to it is selected, so a mapping that selects one of its two ring bonds compares the configuration at that end alone. A common-bond search, in fragments or connected, finds the bonds and atoms below, and its mapping passes validateMapping.
